teaser: A researcher, a curator and a journalist on a schedule, the QR handshake that gives each agent its key, and why it has to be built slowly.
core_idea: The PHP story site is updated by three scheduled agents in a chain, from raw captures to curated evidence to the published site; because neither Claude's scheduled tasks nor ChatGPT gives an agent an identity or a secret, each agent session gets its vault key once by a QR handshake on pki.sgit.ai and is then woken on a schedule, a workflow that is almost working and is being built slowly, in its genesis stage.

nodes.label: Updatability
nodes.summary: When did we last check, and can we prove nothing changed?

nodes.label: The researcher
nodes.summary: Captures pages, raw, into the source watch.

nodes.label: The curator
nodes.summary: Promotes what holds into the evidence vault.

nodes.label: The journalist
nodes.summary: Updates the site and its versioned views.

nodes.label: No identity, no secrets
nodes.summary: Scheduled tasks and ChatGPT have no place for an agent's key.

nodes.label: The QR handshake
nodes.summary: A session key, the root on pki.sgit.ai, one sealed QR image.

nodes.label: A schedule wakes the session
nodes.summary: The same session, still holding its key.

nodes.label: Feature and vulnerability
nodes.summary: A session with a write key acting unattended.

nodes.label: Control is the queue
nodes.summary: The schedule vault: schedules, tasks, run records.

nodes.label: Almost working
nodes.summary: Structure in place; runs not yet all recorded by the agents.

nodes.label: Genesis
nodes.summary: Built slowly by hand, then a product.

quotes.text: It is a slightly mad solution, and a lovely one.
Collection is easy. Collection with an identity, a secret and a schedule is not.
Nothing an agent does on a schedule is outside a task someone queued.
quotes.why: The schedule vault: control is the queue.
